positions.pos: What the sphere grid study found. FFX's standard grid is a ring of seven tracks: each character's section runs into the next, and the last runs back into the first. A locked hub inside the ring is a shortcut that touches six of the seven, not a start. Inside a section the path is long and mostly linear. The labyrinth feeling comes from the closed ring, from locked rewards you can see early, and from rare keys at the seams. The expert grid, where everyone starts in the middle, is the hub and spoke, and the grid you overruled had copied it. This stands unless you flip it.
positions.why: Final Fantasy Wiki, "Sphere Grid": Auron's section "runs into Tidus' grid, thus closing the circle"; Chad Birch, GameInternals (2011): "stretches of over 50 nodes without any branches at all". Source: sprout .specify/specs/ranks-and-badges/research/sphere-grid-study.md (pull request #17)

positions.pos: The grid is rebuilt as a labyrinth on the study's rules. The five streams close a ring in the generating order, and each stream's end runs into the next one's start. Each stream is a home you walk without keys. A small hub inside the ring is a shortcut near four streams, with water left off it, as Auron is in FFX. Locks sit at the seams and before capstones in four key tiers, and the last rank's key opens the hub's capstone. A check holds all of this, and the map is drawn. This stands unless you flip it.

positions.pos: Acknowledge is not a separate button. The player fights with Root's eight trigram moves, and using a move is acknowledging the spirit. Each turn the spirit strikes with a trigram from its stance, and the player answers with a stance and a trigram, as in Root. The right answer is the gate that follows the strike in Root's cycles (Péng, Lǚ, Jǐ, Àn, and Cǎi, Zhǒu, Liè, Kào): it leads the push into emptiness, takes HP from the charge, and gives the player the next move. Any other answer lets the push land. The player's stance against the spirit's stance is the type chart, by the restraining cycle Root already uses. The daemon's name and type show when the first right answer lands. Each daemon strikes with habits drawn from its aim, as Root's nations do, so learning a daemon's habits is the replay; the habit table is a placeholder. This replaces wave-acknowledge-turn. This stands unless you flip it.
positions.why: Your overrule of wave-acknowledge-turn: 'I think this is where we can use the trigrams as moves. The merging of root and the mechanics of spirit battle has the solution I think I'm looking for. Specifically. Using a move IS acknowledging the spirit welcoming is like listening.' Root's rules: sprout root-fight/index.html, 'How it works'. Research: /mnt/project-files/demo/wave-acknowledge-research.md, round 9

positions.pos: Welcome is listening, as Root's lessons teach it: 聽 (ting) is knowing a move has begun, and 懂 (dong) is knowing which gate is coming. A player who Welcomes spends the turn not answering, and the spirit's strike plays slowly and holds before it lands, as on Root's easy tier. As wave-damage has it, that turn's push lands in full. The first Welcome shows the spirit's stance, which is its feeling and element. The second shows which gate is coming, so the next answer can be right. A player who answers without Welcoming reads the strike from the body alone, as on Root's hard tier. The feeling and urge the player offers (wave-spirit-from-charge) still make the spirit. This stands unless you flip it.
positions.why: Your words: 'welcoming is like listening.' Root's Listen and Name the gate lessons teach 聽 and 懂 (root-fight/index.html, lessons 'listen' and 'identify'), and its easy tier holds each strike before it lands.

positions.pos: Validate and Exhale take Root's seize (拿 na). After a right answer the player can keep holding it. Holding is Validate: the player stays with the spirit while its charge drains, and the hold writes its Witness Book page (wave-record). Letting go in the bright window is Exhale. A plain release grounds the charge (wave-release-grounds). Holding from the stance the spirit's feeling feeds is Root's borrowing (借 jie), and an Exhale from there integrates the daemon. Hold too long and the spirit slips free and strikes. This stands unless you flip it.
positions.why: Root's seize: 'keep holding the answer as it lands and you hold the stumbling attacker while their composure drains. Release while the bar is bright to issue... Seize from the stance their channel feeds and you borrow their force' (root-fight/index.html). With moves as Acknowledge and listening as Welcome, seize is the council's reading of the two remaining steps.

A spirit is forest qi gathered around a feeling and has no root to take, so on the strip the same gates answer its weather and let its push spend itself. That is the brother's use, and it frees. research.title: Research you asked for: how to score the asset trial
research.lead: A pass mark is the line you draw before the test. A sample size is how many labelled items you test on. With few items the answer is fuzzy, like judging a baker from five cookies.

items: If the model catches all 5, the true catch rate could still be as low as about 48%.
If it misses 1, the best guess is 80%, and the true rate could be anywhere from about 28% to 99%.
Those two ranges nearly overlap, so five items cannot tell finds-everything from finds-four-of-five.

sections.h: False flags: needs agreeing statements you label
sections.p: If the model flags none of your labelled agreeing statements, the true false-flag rate is probably under:
No pass mark can fix five items, so the mark should be about what the trial can show.

options.label: A. Nearly touching, as the game has them
options.c: The stance stays. The clothes there cannot fit at their cut, so they have to squash where the legs press them (the next question).

options.label: B. About a hand's width apart, 8 to 10 cm
options.c: Root's stance changes so the front legs stand further apart. The clothes may then fit as they are, and the squashing work may not be needed.

research.title: What the cloth prototype found
research.lead: Almost all the cloth that passes through cloth sits in the gap between the two front legs, and that gap is too narrow for the clothes as they are cut.

items: 238 crossing edges at rest in the first meeting: 127 within 12 cm of both front legs, 97 at one front leg, 14 anywhere else.
Most sit 0.5 to 0.6 m up, at the thighs; the pelvis is at 0.63 m.

sections.h: Why no collision method fixed it
items: The front thighs are 3.0 cm apart skin to skin.
Each trouser leg is cut 1.8 cm off the thigh, and its top rows are held by the body.
Each skirt sits outside its own trousers.
So each side needs about 3 cm and both sides about 6 cm, in a 3 cm gap. Every collision variant crossed 222 to 232 times.
One shared cloth pass for both fighters makes the skirts settle when the bodies are still (under 1 cm a step, against 3.8 cm today).
It cuts the cloth step from 33.5 ms to about 4 ms on the test machine.

research.recommend: No recommendation: this is about how the art is practised.

questions.q: Where the two front legs press the clothes between them, should the clothes squash flat onto each wearer's own leg?
questions.why_you: It changes how every garment is built, including the trouser rows now fixed to the body, and how the clothes look up close. How the clothes should look is yours.
questions.not_before: It only became a choice on 2026-10-04, when the prototype showed that no collision method can part clothes cut 6 cm thick in a 3 cm gap.

options.label: A. Yes, squash them where pressed
options.c: Each garment, its held rows included, presses onto its own leg down to a few millimetres where the partner's leg pushes it. This is the answer of the Pixar paper Untangling Cloth for cloth caught between two bodies. It is new garment work.

options.label: B. No, leave the crossing where the camera cannot see it
options.c: Nothing changes in the garments. The cloth check would count only what shows on screen, which first needs a visibility check that does not exist yet.

options.label: C. The stance question is answered first
options.c: If the legs should stand a hand apart, the squashing may not be needed at all.

options.c: Every player starts at the centre. Crossing into a second branch takes a key earned in play, as Final Fantasy X's lock spheres work, so a build feels like a subclass and can still change.

options.label: B. One branch only
options.c: The first refiner to endorse the player sets their branch, and the others stay shut. A build is a fixed subclass, and a second play-through is the way to see another.

options.label: C. Open crossing
options.c: Every branch joins at the centre with no keys. Points alone limit a build, so builds drift toward the same best nodes, and the subclass feeling is weaker.

questions.q: How should the grid carry the spiral and the fractal you see in the sphere grid?
questions.why_you: The study found that no source calls FFX's grid fractal or a spiral: it is a ring of long, mostly linear tracks, drawn so that it winds. Your sense of the grid is the target, and only you can say which form of it you meant.
questions.not_before: Raised by round 5 of the ranks and badges run on 2026-10-04, after the sphere grid study.

options.label: A. The cycle at three scales (recommended, built)
options.c: The five-element cycle turns as the ring of streams, as the five chambers of each stream, and as the five-node loop of each chamber. The grid is truly self-similar, and it teaches the cycle at every scale.

options.label: B. FFX's own way
options.c: Each stream is one long winding track with a few side branches, and the spiral lives in the drawing. Closest to the original; choices come rarely, as the study found in FFX.

options.label: C. A spiral inward
options.c: Each stream winds inward toward the hub, so going deeper means going toward the centre, and the hub's capstone sits at the spiral's end. The fractal is left out.

questions.q: What should walking the Yellow Brick Road feel like to the player? Pick up to three.
questions.why_you: The feature request move asks what satisfaction the work is for, and only you hold yours. The answer sets what the cheap test checks for, and what Act 0 promises. The council leans to triumph and peace, but has no recommendation.
questions.not_before: Raised by the Act 0 and Yellow Brick Road run on 2026-10-05.

options.label: Triumph
options.c: The test checks that an alchemised block feels won, against a real obstacle the player named.

options.label: Peace
options.c: The test checks that the player ends a session settled, with one clear step and nothing nagging.

options.label: Wonder
options.c: The test checks that the pull into Calrunia and the road ahead feel like a world opening.

options.label: Poignance
options.c: The test checks that leaving the game, like Dorothy leaving Oz, carries what the player found there.

options.label: Bliss
options.c: The test checks that the walk feels warm and shared with the allies who walked it.

questions.q: How does the real-world step work, and what does the game keep of the player's life?
questions.why_you: The player's goals and blocks are their own life, and consent and release are reserved to you (council/faces.yaml). The answer sets whether the game stores life answers, where, and whether real life can unlock play. Not asked before because real-life integration was out of scope until your message today.
questions.not_before: Raised by the Act 0 and Yellow Brick Road run on 2026-10-05.

options.label: A. Offered, never gating, kept on the device (recommended)
options.c: At each save the game offers one aligned action for a named goal, like the slice's 'One for your week' card. The player may mark it done; nothing in play depends on it, so nobody is rewarded for lying. Answers stay on the player's device and are never sent.

options.label: B. Real steps unlock play
options.c: Marking a real step done unlocks grid nodes or gold. It ties the game hard to life, and it pays a player to tick boxes, which breaks pillar 3 (skill is bought only with skillful play).

options.label: C. Only at the end
options.c: Play stays in Calrunia. The credits return the player home and hand them their road: the goals, the blocks they alchemised, and one step each. Nothing is asked between sessions.

questions.q: What pulls the traveler out of their world and into Calrunia?
questions.why_you: This is story, and story is yours. It sets Act 0's last scene and who the traveler first owes. Not asked before because Act 0 did not exist.
questions.not_before: Raised by the Act 0 and Yellow Brick Road run on 2026-10-05.

options.label: A. The brother's call, answered by choice (recommended)
options.c: The brother 'can only use people who choose it' and leaves breadcrumbs (design.md, 'The brother'). In Act 0 his breadcrumbs reach the player's world, and stepping through is the player's choice. It makes the brother the hidden reason the traveler is there, paid off in the cave.

options.label: B. An accident, like Dorothy's storm
options.c: The player is swept in with no choice. Closest to Oz; nobody in Calrunia meant it, so the traveler owes no one.

options.label: C. The game is the door
options.c: In Act 0 the player starts a game called Sprout Plot on a screen, and it takes them in. Playful and honest about being a game, but it sits outside the world's own story.

questions.q: Which domains does Act 0 ask the player's goals in?
questions.why_you: You overruled ya-intake: the five channel domains flavour what each channel teaches and its starting village, and the intake should follow the Allyship domains or the Lenses domains. The Allyship domains are in the record; the Lenses domains are not in any repo, so only you hold them. The rest of the intake stands as drafted: the player picks a goal and the block in its way from the six beliefs, and types nothing.
questions.not_before: Raised by your steer on ya-intake, 2026-10-05.

options.label: A. Mastering Allyship's four domains (recommended until we see Lenses)
options.c: Gather Resources, Skillful Organizing, Direct Action, Raise Awareness (mtgoa Appendix A). A goal names the kind of action the player wants to take in their life. The book's daemon affinity table already links each domain to the blocks.

options.label: B. The Lenses domains
options.c: The intake asks in the Lenses domains. Please paste or describe them in the steer box, and the council builds the intake from them in round 3.

options.label: C. Both, Lenses for where and Allyship for how
options.c: The player names a life area from the Lenses domains and the kind of action from the four Allyship domains. Two picks per goal. Please paste the Lenses domains in the steer box.

questions.q: How should the gold from a player's block reach the grid?
questions.why_you: You stood pr-inner-demons (spoils of the node's element activate it) and ya-grid-pace (the road is as long as the blocks the player alchemises). The test shows the two cannot both hold: every chamber of the grid asks for all five elements in turn, so a player who names one block is short of the other four. Choosing between your two rulings is yours.
questions.not_before: Raised by the Act 0 falsify test on 2026-10-05 (sprout tools/test-act-zero.mjs).

options.label: A. Gold is gold (recommended)
options.c: Grounding any charge, or a real step, yields gold that activates any node; the node's element still sets its stats. Lead becomes gold, as the alchemy says. It amends pr-inner-demons. In the test this passed every check: integrated play walked 31 nodes, story and prompted play 25, and doubling the named block's charges moved the grid from 25 to 32.

options.label: B. Keep spoils of the node's element
options.c: pr-inner-demons stays as it stands. The named block flavours the encounters and the cards but does not pace the road, and integrated play's step gold is paid in whichever element the next node needs rather than the block's. In the test, as stood, a named block slowed the road (14.7 nodes against 20.5 with none).

questions.q: Which part of the game should the first playable demo cover?
questions.why_you: Who the demo is for and how far a stranger should get are yours; the record holds the slice and the acts but no demo. The answer sets every number in the scope map: how many spirits, scenes, quests and maps get built first.
questions.not_before: Raised by your message of 2026-10-06 asking what a working demo would take.

options.label: A. Act 0 through the first call (recommended)
options.c: About an hour. Pulled into Calrunia, life in the settlement, hunter status, the strip, the first ally and the ring opening. Needs the five first spirits, the settlement, 12 quests and about 8 scenes. No Act II content.

options.label: B. Act 0, a short Act I, and a taste of Act II
options.c: Compresses Act I to its loops and ends at the crossing, one village and cave chamber 1. Shows more of the world, but needs a village, cave art and Act II spirits on top of A, and the exile lands without the time spent earning it.

options.label: C. Act 0 and the strip only
options.c: About twenty minutes: the pull, the creator, the intake and the encounter loop on the strip with the five spirits. Fastest to ship; no settlement, quests or orientation walk yet.

questions.q: How should the scene editor let you change a staged scene?
questions.why_you: You asked for a scene editor, and your staging ruling (fr-staging-lead) asked for scenes from a script with no hand placement. Whether the editor keeps that rule or lets you place by hand is your preference, and it decides what the editor writes.
questions.not_before: Raised by your message of 2026-10-06; the staging spec has no editor.

options.label: A. A timeline that writes beats into the script (recommended)
options.c: You watch a scene, scrub it, and add a camera move, a mark or a pause; the change is saved in the script as a beat, and the stager stays the one placer, so an edit survives every rebuild.

options.label: B. Hand placement, like RPG Maker's event editor
options.c: You drag figures and the camera on the map and the positions are saved. Full control, but every map change can break a placed scene, and it amends your no-hand-placement ruling.

options.label: C. No editor yet
options.c: Scripts and the stager only; you review by watching and steering in words. Cheapest now; the editor waits until there are enough scenes to need it.

questions.q: How should the game work a blocked WAVE step?
questions.why_you: It is a choice about what the practice is. The record holds the game's own block cycle, and your self-sabotage ruling points toward meeting the voice in the way. The Shaman dissents from the other faces here.
questions.not_before: The blocked step did not exist until your note of 6 October. Meanwhile the build runs on A, and B or C would replace only the block work, not the return or the map.

options.label: A. Through the game's own cycle (recommended)
options.c: The player finds the block in the body, names its channel and face, holds a true belief until it shifts, then returns to the step. It builds now on the engine the game already has.

options.label: B. Through a smaller WAVE on the block
options.c: The player welcomes and breathes with what is in the way, then returns. Quicker and gentler, and it never names a channel or a face.

options.label: C. By meeting the voice that is blocking
options.c: A short interview with the daemon in the way (its job, who it works for, whether it will step aside), then the return. Closest to Big Mind, and it waits on the daemon ontology you have not ruled yet.

questions.q: In what order do the 247 Kickstarter backers get their books across the batches?
questions.why_you: The order decides which named people wait longest, and anything that names a person is reserved to you. Nothing in the record ranks the backers.
questions.not_before: One shipment needed no order. Rolling batches, chosen today, do.

options.c: Every backer can check their place against their own pledge, and the message before batch one tells each person roughly which month is theirs.

options.c: The people owed the most get their books first, about eight months in. Everyone else starts after them, which the message has to say plainly.

options.label: A fresh draw each batch
options.c: Nobody's place is fixed by when they pledged. Nobody can know their month in advance, so the message can only give the cadence.

questions.q: At the budget's pace of 7 or 8 backer books a month, the last backer gets a book in mid to late 2029. Do you keep that pace?
questions.why_you: Each faster option moves money between budget lines or slows paying back the family contribution, and money is reserved to you. It may also need the Volunteer CFO's agreement under the /ally/mom terms.
questions.not_before: The per-copy figures and the queue length were first put side by side in this pass. The $0.50 to $1.50 a copy for shipping a batch is the council's estimate, and batch one's KDP cart gives the real number.

options.label: Keep the budget's pace, and raise it at the weekly review as income arrives (recommended)
options.c: Batch one ships as budgeted and the message tells backers the cadence. The Challenger dissents: it would recycle sale revenue from batch one.

options.label: Put part of every $40 sale back into backer copies
options.c: The queue shortens with every sale, and family repayment slows by the same amount. The council asks you for the share in the next round.

options.label: Send backer copies straight from KDP, using the $10.40 allowance for KDP's shipping

steers_recorded.text: Do research on the developmental levels the faces are built off of. Spiral dynamics and integral theory and see if there are any projects that also use agents in this way
On pipe-steps-page: I think a tab on this board is quite useful

On daemon-subagents-purpose: The daemons exist to solve problems in the faces domain. They are designed to protect the player but also all work for the players enjoyment. They should be able to ask questions and help with specific problems
On dm-no-chains: This we could explore. I don't see it's utility now but I imagine the diplomat would appreciate the collaboration
On iching-cast-first: We don't need them evenly. We actually want to do a simulation of the coin method and then map to the reading
Context: Everyone in the character creation should be building out a Taoist cultivation robe set and so our roles have to fit into that aesthetic

On pr-act3-sources: Let’s call the project a quest. We also want to think about the game in terms of encounters quests adventures and campaigns  

A project would be an adventure (which is a series of quests and encounters) to attain the last rank 

This also allows for post main story progress to continue
On pr-reservations: Nodes in final fantasy branch off in different paths to simulate the idea of different subclasses for the character. I want to preserve that feeling

On pr-test-result: I need to know what the implications of this are. We want to steal the scouting structure but we’ll let the games needs decided how many badges. Paper Mario also has a lot of badges as well. And the available badges in BSA is larger than the required amount
On pr-last-rank-adventure: The whole game uses these terms not just the last adventure

On pr-grid-built (said in chat): On the council board I need to be able to “go back” if I overrule without context (like I just did) 

The context is here. The sphere grid works because it acts as a labyrinth not hub and spoke. The path spirals and fractals. We need to do a study of how the sphere grid operates to get a clearer picture of this

On pr-branch-emphasis: Branches aren’t based on stats like the sphere grid branches unlock moves and the specific build of stats that would support the subtype of the type of character you’re building as you traverse the path

On pr-labyrinth-scale: Something between a and c. The cycle inward connects to the world ring concept- the idea of fighting inner demons for development resonates and using the spoils of those fights for advancement

On ya-feeling: Really walking the yellow brick road should afford all 6 feelings because they are all gold bricks, but triumph wonder and poignance are the ones I want to feel in designing and implementing this
On ya-real-steps: honestly I think all three are necessary. [...] different modes of play that players can switch throuh [...] the modeas can be shifted in the middle fo play throughs

On ya-intake (overruled): I think we need to think about domains a bit more. These are what the different channels teach you and flavors their starting village, but the domains should be more aligned with the Allyship domains or the LEnses Domains (which I can provide context on)

On ya-domains (C): The lenses domains haven't been formalized, but if the Allyship Domains are about helping other people the lenses domains could be seen about helping one's self. But really it's about life domains, Relationships, Career, Money, Creativity etc. I think players can choose which ones where they don't get to choose in the same way re: allyship
On ya-three-modes: "and asks for nothing outside the game." well they ask for information about the players life outside of the game.
On demo-spirit-count: "We need to also include the daemons. 8 x 5 x 3 (approximately)"
On demo-settlement-size: "I think argyra should be bigger. Think saffron city from pokemon. The idea is that there will be MANY NPCs and side quests "
On enc-who-carries: "I think all the beliefs can be applied to each of the daemons "

On enc-steady-rests: "This should be more like pokemon battles where the moves do HP to the daemon and each of the moves is an inner move the player can do to get the emotional alchemy effects in themselves. WAVE is a good example of this."

On enc-inner-moves: "Not all moves take HP away. I think if we are going to use WAVE as the main loop we should explore what each step does as it connects to the basic integral moves 

(Wake up open up clean up grow up and show up )"

On enc-wave-set: "I think welcome allows the player to see what the opponent actually is. We need a way for a random charge to emerge and by going through the game the players see what type of enemy is emerging

For instance the acknowledge phase would be where the spirit would get a name

Validate would add it to a record of spirits the player has encountered and is working through like a pokedex 

Exhale could be release the spirit OR integrate the spirit (express)

I think I want to do a full brainstorm on how these mechanics could work "
On enc-moves-from-grid: "This is close but a little too clunky. The spirit is there but I want to think more deeply about it "
On oag-block-work: "Mix of a and c"

On oag-wave-depth: "I do think we should cap the depth so players don’t get lost in the minutiae. We can have a notice that lets them know they are going in too deep and they might next external support about it and maybe a link to booking a call with me "
On ship-order: "The people who raise their hand first with an updated address get their books faster "
I want to make sure the work from the morning brief is coming into the council board as well

battles.name: Scene Staging
battles.intro: It wants a scene script to play itself: the people of a scene stand, walk and speak in the chamber the script names, with no hand placement. Today the cave's eight chambers are built and named on the map, and the slice can walk and show a line of text, but nobody else stands on the map and nothing starts a scene.

battles.name: Character Creation
battles.intro: It wants the people of the world to have looks of their own: healers, elders, hunters and villagers built from the character parts, inside the sprite budget.

battles.name: Ranks and Badges
battles.intro: It wants progression to be a rank ladder like Scouting's, with badges won like Pokémon's and worn like Paper Mario's, and a grid where the player spends what play earned, like Final Fantasy X.

battles.name: Act 0 and the Yellow Brick Road
battles.intro: It wants the game to begin in the player's own world, ask what life they want after the game, pull them into Calrunia, and turn every forest encounter into lead becoming gold, so the grid charts their road and they walk it home.

battles.name: A demo people can play
battles.intro: It wants a working demo strangers can try: more spirits and a number for them, a settlement that feels alive with quests and an orientation, and a scene editor for cinematic 2D cutscenes.

battles.name: Shipping the Book
battles.intro: It wants the backers who funded Mastering the Game of Allyship to get their books in rolling KDP batches, paced by the /ally/mom budget, and told the truth about the wait.

battles.name: Launching the Podcast
battles.intro: It wants the Flirtcraft podcast heard: episode 1 on Spotify with its own cover art, and a page on the Flirtcraft site where people find it. The page is live at /podcast. Spotify for Creators hosts the show, the cover follows Mastering Allyship's look, and the episode's title is drafted from the audio.

battles.name: Orienting New Players
battles.intro: It wants a stranger to understand the Flirtcraft game and leave each rep with one move to make. Today the free run teaches the loop in plain words, and the paid seven-step run deals up to five moves and about twenty unexplained terms. The six audited the loop and the jump between the two.

battles.name: Writing the Book
battles.intro: It wants a Flirtcraft book that teaches the game in the game's own loop and words. The outline is drafted: seven parts and twenty-seven chapters, built on one rep, with the eight crafts in the order of service.

battles.name: Episode 2 with Tom
battles.intro: It wants episode 2 of the Mastering the Game of Allyship podcast out on YouTube, with Tom Hurlburt: a title, a description with chapters, and a thumbnail. The council drafted them from the transcript, and thumbnails are now a step of every episode.

battles.name: Coaching site as a game
battles.intro: It wants your coaching site to be a game that people play through to reach the help they need from you. The council built it on your five moves, with a sentence to keep at every stop and the booking always one tap away.
